transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you're all aware, we had a roof leak overnight that exposed 1,200 electric-motor housings in finished-goods storage. The housings are on four pallets of 300 units each — P1, P2, P3, and P4. Our customer's Monday assembly schedule depends on these housings, so we need to move quickly but correctly. Per our standard process, we need to hold a quality-and-warehouse disposition huddle before any water-exposed material is released or discarded. I'd like to get that started now. Quality and Warehouse, please enter your complete current findings into the disposition record — including all measured results and required controls, or formally record that you have no finding. Once both function entries are complete, I'll summarize the agreed disposition and issue the formal decision. Let's hear what we know so far.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My electrical laboratory report is pending my sign-off before upload to the quality system, but I can share it now. The report covers the 600 housings on P2 and P4: 540 passed insulation testing and 60 failed. The 540 passing units may be released only after 100% insulation testing is recorded, while the 60 failed units must be scrapped.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: This is Elena, Warehouse. My warehouse inspection log — still awaiting inventory reconciliation — identifies P2 and P4 as the only pallets that received direct water exposure. Those 600 units correspond to Jon's tested lot. The dry room can process them in exactly 6 hours before release, so P2 and P4 must remain segregated during drying. P1 and P3 were not directly exposed and, per our disposition procedure, should be treated as unaffected and releasable. That completes my warehouse entry for the disposition record.
transcript.speaker: A3
